newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom's Vyakhirev criticises reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom's Vyakhirev criticises reform plan.

text.p: Rem Vyakhirev, the chairman of Russia's natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom, accused U.S. oil and gas interests on Wednesday of being behind plans to restructure the company.

Vyakhirev told the State Duma lower house of parliament that U.S. companies were acting through the ministry of finance and International Monetary Fund to introduce the reforms, which he said would not cure Russia's problems.

"The proposed measures for structural reform in the (natural) gas industry... will result in the creation of monopolies in different spheres of activity which won't compete with one another," a prepared text of Vyakhirev's speech said.
"In all instances those kinds of measures will most likely raise expenditure on power sources."

The IMF has urged Russia to reform its natural monopolies -- monolithic industries such as gas, electricity, oil pipelines and rail where there are no competitors -- and the new reformist cabinet has made restructuring them a priority.

First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov has said the monopolies will not be broken up, although he will seek tighter state regulation and a redistribution of the tariff burden between enterprises and consumers.
Last week he said the goal of restructuring Gazprom should be the provision of a single transport tariff and that the company should face competition to exploit new reserves.
Vyakhirev said it was still too early for price reforms.
"The system of setting prices and the order for determining excises should not be destroyed until production and payments in the Russian economy have stabilised," Vyakhirev said.
He said only 50 percent of 1996-97 gas deliveries to consumers had been paid for although gas prices for industry were 2.5 to three times lower in Russia than in Western Europe.
He recommended a gradual transition to shield poorer citizens from a sudden price hike.

He pointed to initiatives Gazprom was already implementing to improve its organisation, including moving to a centralised system of accounting for gas transport and separating production from other operations.
The Duma later passed a non-binding resolution calling on the government not to break up Gazprom or Russia's gas network.
